decisions.quote: While the replicated estimate of the difference in predicted probabilities is nearly identical to that of the original study (0.098 vs 0.097), levels exhibit small differences: 0.649 vs 0.608 for union members and 0.552 vs 0.511 for the nonunion members. Because these differences remain small (about 4 percentage points or 6–7 percent in relative terms), they can be attributed to the discrepancies between the reproduction and original regression samples.
decisions.location: Control variable coefficient(s) in focal model (lines 112-116); Reproduction Result (lines 78-104)
decisions.reason: Under the codebook rules for outcome_computation, 'computationally reproducible' requires that the original reported numbers be obtained again up to rounding and negligible numerical differences, whereas 'computational issues' applies when the analysis ran and produced numbers but the original numbers could not be recovered. Here, reconstructing the dataset from the underlying ESS and auxiliary data yielded an unresolved sample discrepancy (18 country-years and 8,174 observations vs. 34 country-years and 19,296 observations in the original study, driven by ~10 percentage-point differences in low-income inclusiveness), shifted the predicted probability levels in Table 4 by ~4 percentage points / 6–7% (0.649 vs. 0.608 for union members and 0.552 vs. 0.511 for nonunion members), and slightly changed their difference (0.098 vs. 0.097). Although the focal claim met the SCORE replication criteria because both predicted probabilities shifted upward by the same amount, the original numbers were not computationally recovered, supporting 'computational issues'.
